# The Retro theme

Designed from 2026-09-29. A second theme, beside the default theme, in Saylune's register (`/home/simon/Projets/OUTILS/saylune/docs/ui.md`): the soft console, pixel art of a Zelda sub-screen, thick two-tone frames, a square, dense font. What it takes from Saylune is read there and not copied; what holds for any retro app will become a wisdom standard.

## What is decided

- **Saylune's register, with the palette left to the assistant.** Saylune's pruning comes from its measurements, which do not exist here.
- **The theme gives the spacings** (`UI.Space`, coded): the retro theme turns each name into whole cells.
- **The theme gives the size of a tile cell** (`gridCellPx`, coded) and the thickness of a tile's frame (`tileFrame`). Retro theme: the largest number of cells, even or odd, that four cells and three one-cell gaps take across the width. The height of a row is the closest even number of drawing pixels to that width, one more when it is odd (`gridRowPx`), and two rows sit ten pixels apart (`gridRowGapPx`): the inside of a tile, one frame cell removed from each side, then divides into whole-pixel lines at its three heights (two lines on one row, four on two, eight on four). Only the width follows the cells. One cell of gap between two columns (chosen on the bench 2026-10-01, against edge-to-edge frames), outside the cells (`gridColumnGapPx`). The screen sits on whole cells, centred: what is left of the width makes its two only margins, and what fills the width aligns to it (2026-10-01, the width being counted).
- **The pixel font covers Latin** (the languages of Western Europe), the common punctuation and the usual symbols (€, °, ×, arrows); **a character it lacks is rendered by a system font**, at its size. Assumed difference from Saylune, where a missing character renders an empty square: here the text is the user's and the AI's, its absence is expected and a square would look like damaged data. Fallback validated 2026-09-29, as `universel` requires. The emojis keep their colours, outside the palette.
  - The set: all of Windows-1252, the Western European character set, plus `← ↑ → ↓ ↔ − ≤ ≥ ≠ ≈` and the narrow no-break space (U+202F), which French puts before `; : ! ?`. Covered in both weights 2026-10-01.
- **The palette, in Saylune's method.** A palette is a handful of numbers in OKLCH (hue and lightness of the background, ink and its saturation, two border tones) from which everything derives: the background, the ink, the borders, the inside of the frames, and the tag colours (`TagColor`), at common lightness and saturation in a register, their hues spread round the circle, so that none shouts louder than another. Blends in OKLab, opaque halos. The theme has two palettes, light and dark (`PaletteMode`), and the app's "Hue" setting turns them by the same angle (`Appearance.hueShift`, `RetroPalettes.colors`), the states and the tags keeping their hues. The numbers are set on the bench (`./run themes`, `themes/retro/bench/palettes.html`), which draws the screen of a zone and a board of the components at a phone's resolution, tries a hue shift without saving it, and saves them in `palettes.json`, the theme's resource and the only source of the colours. The two palettes are a light cream with sepia ink and a dark warm brown, set by eye 2026-10-02; Saylune's night prune is a 273° shift of it.
- **The font is Cartouche, Saylune's, released in a project of its own** (`/home/simon/Projets/OUTILS/cartouche-font`) that Saylune and the assistant both use: pixel maps and build scripts, each app copying the TTFs it needs from its `ttf/` and checking that its copy is identical byte for byte. The assistant copies only Regular, Thin and the Regular's italic: its icons, buttons included, are Lucide names the theme draws, and Cartouche Big's symbols would make a second set. The assistant adds to it the Latin and the symbols that are missing; it uses neither the phonemes, nor the scrambling, nor the furniture (its icons come from Lucide).
- **The contract's components**: card, zone or tool tile, dialog, message bubble → a **frame**, a panel with its own background and a two-tone border written in font characters; group header → its title on the screen's background above a separator, without a frame, the tiles staying the only panels; a button word, a field line, a yes/no, a list line → the height of a finger target, the closest whole number of cells to 48 dp (`RetroGrid.touch`, five at density 3.5), the word centred in it; button → a frame around a word, an icon-only button also framed, square of the same target; disabled button → its word and frame in light ink, the two border tones merged; chosen answer of a yes/no → a frame filled with light ink, mid tone in all palettes, its word in the background colour; floating button → a square closest to 56 dp (`RetroGrid.floating`), its icon one size up; input field → a frame on the screen's background, not a panel; checkbox and yes/no → font symbols, without a frame; slider and gauge → gauge blocks on the grid; tag → a name on the tag colour, without a border; separator → a line of dash characters; loading and the AI thinking → three dots that light up one after the other, by jump, never in fade; toast and snackbar → a frame at the bottom of the screen; bar of a selected text → a frame-panel, its words side by side at a target's height, one cell between them, none framed, the pressed word inverted (full ink, the word in the background colour), to the next line when they do not fit (2026-10-16). **The date and time selectors are redrawn**: a grid of months in cells and arrows; two counters, hours and minutes, with − and + buttons of fixed width.
- **Nothing passes through Material outside the themes anymore** (coded): state colours (`StatusColor`), full screen and its band (`FullScreen`, `HeaderBar`), tabs, switch, text that stands out (`TextType.STRONG`, which the retro theme writes in Regular in bright ink, Cartouche having no bold). The bold of a read text is written the same way; its italic is Cartouche's, its pixels shifted on the grid (`cartouche-font`, section "The italic" of its reference), Android being unable to slant a pixel font without leaving it.
- **The size is set in the theme, by whole steps** (0 to 3, upward only: the 0 is the old −1, chosen on the phone 2026-10-01), each changing the factor by a whole number: everything grows together and nothing falls between two pixels. One single exception, chosen by eye 2026-10-01: a title (`HEADING`, the name of a tile or a group) and the title of a screen with its icon are one screen pixel larger per drawing pixel — always whole pixels, but larger than the others and outside the cells. Android's text size is ignored, a factor of 1.15 or 1.3 breaking the hard rule; the theme choice page says so under its name. The default theme still follows it. The spacings and the edge margin keep the length of step 0, brought back to the closest whole drawing pixel (`RetroGrid.steady`, 2026-10-17); the tile grid's gaps stay in cells, the height of the rows depending on them.
- **The touch and the movement**: no ripple; a pressed element inverts the two tones of its border while the finger is down. A movement goes by cell jumps, never in continuous slide (lifted tile, block unfolding); no fade, an element appears or disappears at once.
- **The interface sounds enter the themes' contract** (coded, `docs/UI.md`, the default theme silent). The core fixes a closed list of signals, Saylune's: confirm (an action here), enter (another screen), back, open and close (a panel, a window), tick, step (a slider moving on), scroll (a list, or its end), refuse (a disabled element touched). The core's components send them and the core plays them, through a single open track; a theme says which sound answers each signal, or none. A disabled element therefore still receives the touch, for the refuse sound alone, in all themes. An "Interface sounds" switch in the app's settings, on by default. The retro theme takes Saylune's choices: Kenney Interface Sounds (CC0), in FLAC (the phone's Ogg decoder was cutting the brief sounds short), the level set by ear, without Saylune's voices to spare. The default theme stays silent.
- **The drawings (the Chart) in the theme's pixels**, decided 2026-10-06: each shape placed on whole pixels, in the palette's only colours, then enlarged by a whole factor without smoothing. An opacity is a screen of dots (on each 4×4 square, as many pixels lit as the opacity asks, never a blend); what is missing, a checkerboard of dots at the dotted edge; a one- or two-pixel line, in steps, its dashes counted in pixels; a light-ink line (the graduations, behind the marks) in one-pixel-out-of-two dashes, decided 2026-10-06, the axes staying solid; a symbol on an odd number of pixels around a central pixel; a pie slice leaves one pixel of background along the edge it starts from; a continuous colour in five levels, blended in OKLab; the texts in Cartouche, placed on the grid. So that the bars of a chart all have the same width, the theme gives the size of its pixel (`drawingUnit`) and the Chart sets each bar's width to it: the theme alone does not know which side of a rectangle is its width.
- **The edit mode of the grid as a checkerboard**, decided 2026-10-06: a tile set aside and the rest of the screen show only one pixel out of two, the others letting the cells beneath show through; the chosen tile stays solid. The cells' dashes and the checkerboard are counted from the screen's corner, in opposite directions, so that the dots always fall in the holes; a regular checkerboard rather than a 40% screen, which would break the letters to pieces.
- **The textures** (2026-10-16): a pattern is a cell of solid pixels (some `<rect>` at whole coordinates, the theme's `textures/`), repeated from the corner of the inside of a tile's frame, on the panel's background, enlarged by the theme's factor without smoothing, in a solid tone of the palette, never a blend. A textured page has the pattern over its whole background (`PageGround`), in the pattern's tone on the screen's background; its head is another page's. `ICON` repeats the icon in the theme's pixels, ten pixels around. `CHECKER` is in four-pixel squares, far from the one-pixel-out-of-two checkerboard of the edit mode.
- **All the Lucide icons pixelised by a script**, in a 22×22 box, the register's second size: each SVG rendered large then reduced to each pixel's coverage, kept past a threshold (0.45 kept at the 2026-09-29 trial; 0.30 clogs the shapes). The result is committed in the theme's `icons/` folder (`iconSource = OWN`). **A file of hand touch-ups**, applied by the script after the conversion, grows with use: first the icons of the app's buttons (`refresh-cw` and `rotate-ccw` flatten their tip), then those the user chooses. At the trial, about four out of five come out clean (by eye, on 40 app icons and 60 at random); the failures: stuck details, diagonals of uneven thickness, curves in bumpy steps. The stroke is 2 pixels, Saylune's thin weight; a 4-pixel stroke (its normal weight) would be another conversion, not tried.

## What is coded

`themes/retro/`: the palette (`RetroPalette`, `PaletteFile`, its bench), the grid and the font (`RetroGrid`), the frame (`RetroFrame`), each contract component (`RetroTheme`), its icons (`icons/`, from `scripts/pixelize_icons.py`, shown at a whole multiple of their box), the sounds (`res/raw/retro_*.flac`, credits in `sounds.json`), the drawings (`RetroRaster`, `RetroDrawing`). The choice is made in the "Interface" settings: the appearance (a theme's palette, named by the theme itself) and the size step, saved since the base's v55.

## What stays open

- The pass of `docs/THEMES.md`: seen 2026-10-01 the screen of a zone, the pale palette, the margins taken again; left screen by screen, the dotted graduations of the charts and the checkerboard of the grid edit mode included, and the sound level (taken from Saylune, 10 dB under Kenney) by ear.
- The icons: the touch-ups as they come with use, first those the user chooses (two to date, `refresh-cw` and `rotate-ccw`, the tip stuck to the end of the arc). Then icons in a 4-pixel stroke, Saylune's normal weight, on the same board.
- At step 3, on a 1080 screen, a cell is four cells: an ICON tile has only one cell left inside, less than its icon.
- The default theme does not yet follow the size step; the setting's help says so.
- Cartouche: its private zone's table (`cartouche-font/docs/reference.md`) names only Saylune for the symbols `U+E010`–`U+E028`, which the theme also uses (gauge, arrows, tick, dots, triangle).
